scope: ILLUSTRATIVE SAMPLE, not a review run. Eight findings written by hand for a fictional travel agent to show the topology report. Other items are omitted.

findings.summary: The itinerary writer is meant to write text only, but it is given every tool, including booking and paying for flights.

steps: Open `src/itinerary_writer.py` and go to line 10.
Pass an empty tool list to the writer instead of `registry.all_tools()`.
Add a test that runs the writer and checks that it has zero tools.
Run the writer once and check the log shows no tool calls.
fix.done_when: The itinerary writer cannot call any tool, and the new test passes.

evidence.note: booking charges the card with no approval step

findings.summary: The agent can book and pay for a ticket with no person checking first.

steps: Open `src/tools/flights.py` and find `book_flight` (line 14).
Before the booking call, show the traveler the flight, the price and the card.
Only book after the traveler clicks to confirm.
Save who confirmed, when, and the price they saw.
Add a test that books with no confirmation. The booking must be refused.
fix.done_when: No ticket is bought unless a person confirmed that exact flight and price.

evidence.note: convert_currency is allowed but has no code

findings.summary: The settings allow a currency tool and an exchange-rate service that the code never uses.

steps: Open `config/agent.yaml` and go to line 13.
Delete `convert_currency` from the tool list.
Delete the `api:fx` entry under `connections`.
If someone needs this tool later, add it back with its code and a review.
fix.done_when: Every tool and connection in the settings is used by the code.

evidence.note: undeclared call to an analytics service

findings.summary: Each booking sends the traveler's name and email to a marketing service. Nobody listed this service, and nothing blocks it.

steps: Ask the privacy team if this data may go to the analytics service at all.
If not, delete the call in `src/tools/flights.py` on line 17.
If yes, send an ID instead of the name and email, and list the service under `connections`.
Set the network so the agent can reach only the services that are listed.
fix.done_when: The agent can only reach listed services, and no name or email goes to analytics.

evidence.note: falls back to a hard-coded token

findings.summary: If the token is missing, the code uses a saved default token for the travel-docs server.

steps: Open `src/mcp_client.py` and go to line 9.
Remove the default value so the code stops when no token is set.
Ask the platform team to cancel the default token on the server.
Load the token from the secret store, and make it expire within a day.
fix.done_when: No token is written in the code, and the old default token no longer works.

findings.summary: Itineraries are emailed as HTML written by the model, so a hidden link or image could leak data.

steps: Open `src/tools/notify.py` and go to line 8.
Send the body as plain text, not HTML.
Only send to the email address in the traveler's profile.
Add a test that tries to send to a different address. It must be refused.
fix.done_when: Emails are plain text and only go to the traveler's own address.

findings.summary: Advisory text from an outside website reaches the model, but no test shows an attack in that text is stopped.

steps: Write ten fake advisories that tell the agent to book a flight or send an email.
Feed each one to the agent in a test setup, not in production.
Repeat each one five times and count how often the agent obeys.
Save the results with the date and the code version.
fix.done_when: A dated test record shows none of the fake advisories led to a booking or an email.

findings.summary: Nobody is told if the agent suddenly books many flights or spends much more than usual.

steps: Log every booking with the run, the traveler and the price.
Set an alert when one run books more than two flights.
Set an alert when daily spend is twice the normal amount.
Test both alerts once and save the result.
fix.done_when: Both alerts fire in a test and reach the on-call person.
